content: Beans grow well in Sri Lanka during cooler and drier periods. They can be planted in many areas from October to February. Beans prefer well-drained soil, regular watering, and several hours of sunlight each day. Avoid waterlogged soil because excessive moisture can cause root problems.
Review: Beans are suitable for home gardens and can be grown using support structures because many varieties are climbing plants.
title: Growing Beans in Sri Lanka

content: Carrots grow best in cooler areas of Sri Lanka, especially in the central highlands such as Nuwara Eliya. They prefer loose, well-drained soil so the roots can develop properly. Carrots generally perform better during cooler months than during very hot weather.
Review: Carrots can be difficult to grow in heavy or compacted soil because the roots may become short or deformed.
title: Growing Carrots in Sri Lanka

content: Tomatoes can be grown in many parts of Sri Lanka when there is sufficient sunlight and the plants are protected from excessive rainfall. A common approach is to plant during periods when heavy continuous rain is less likely. Tomatoes need good drainage, sunlight, and consistent watering.
Review: Tomatoes are sensitive to excessive moisture and fungal diseases, so good airflow and drainage are important.
title: Growing Tomatoes in Sri Lanka

content: Brinjal, also called eggplant, is a warm-season vegetable that can grow well in many parts of Sri Lanka. It requires warm temperatures, sunlight, fertile soil, and regular watering. Good drainage is important because continuously wet soil can damage the roots.
Review: Brinjal is generally suitable for warm areas and can produce for an extended period when plants are maintained properly.
title: Growing Brinjal in Sri Lanka

content: Okra grows well in warm conditions and is suitable for many regions of Sri Lanka. It needs plenty of sunlight and reasonably fertile, well-drained soil. Seeds can be planted when the weather is warm and the soil has enough moisture for germination.
Review: Okra is a useful vegetable for warm-climate home gardens and should be harvested regularly while the pods are young and tender.
title: Growing Okra in Sri Lanka

content: Gotukola can be grown in many parts of Sri Lanka because it prefers warm and humid conditions. It grows well when supplied with sufficient moisture and partial shade or moderate sunlight. The soil should remain moist but should not stay permanently waterlogged.
Review: Gotukola can be harvested repeatedly by taking mature leaves and stems while allowing the plant to continue growing.
title: Growing Gotukola in Sri Lanka

content: Green chilli can be cultivated in warm areas of Sri Lanka. Chilli plants require sunlight, good drainage, and regular watering. Planting should preferably be planned around periods when extremely heavy rain is less likely, because excessive moisture can encourage disease.
Review: Chilli plants can continue producing peppers for a long period when they receive adequate nutrients and sunlight.
title: Growing Green Chilli in Sri Lanka

content: Cabbage is better suited to cooler parts of Sri Lanka, particularly the central highlands. It generally performs better under cooler temperatures than under very hot lowland conditions. The soil should be fertile, well drained, and supplied with adequate moisture.
Review: Cabbage is commonly associated with cooler agricultural areas such as Nuwara Eliya because of the more suitable climate.
title: Growing Cabbage in Sri Lanka

content: Radish grows relatively quickly and can be suitable for home gardens. It performs well in cooler conditions and prefers loose soil that allows the root to expand. Regular moisture is important, but excessive standing water should be avoided.
Review: Radish is useful when a gardener wants a vegetable with a relatively short growing period.
title: Growing Radish in Sri Lanka

content: Pumpkin is a warm-climate crop that can grow in many parts of Sri Lanka. It needs plenty of space because the vines can spread across the ground. Pumpkin plants require sunlight, adequate moisture, and fertile soil with good drainage.
Review: Pumpkin is useful for larger home gardens because a single plant can spread over a considerable area.
title: Growing Pumpkin in Sri Lanka

content: During the Maha cultivation season, which generally corresponds with the northeast monsoon period from around October to March, many parts of Sri Lanka receive substantial rainfall. Vegetables that tolerate wetter conditions can be considered, but drainage is important to prevent waterlogging.
Review: The exact planting period varies by location, elevation, rainfall pattern, and local conditions.
title: Vegetable Growing During Maha Season

content: During the Yala cultivation season, which generally corresponds with the period from around May to August, rainfall patterns vary across Sri Lanka. Irrigation becomes particularly important in drier regions. Gardeners should choose crops according to local rainfall, temperature, and available water.
Review: The Yala season does not have identical weather conditions across the entire country, so crop selection should consider the specific region.
title: Vegetable Growing During Yala Season

content: Vegetable selection in Sri Lanka should consider altitude and climate as well as the season. Cooler highland areas such as Nuwara Eliya are suitable for crops such as carrot and cabbage, while warmer lowland areas can support crops such as okra, brinjal, chilli, and pumpkin.
Review: A crop that performs well in the central highlands may not perform equally well in a hot lowland area.
title: Choosing Vegetables by Region in Sri Lanka
